thread:
ana (ux): dropping a new flow for the latency observability page — main changes: compact time-range presets, a responsive heatmap that folds into a mini-sparkline on narrow width, and an inline p95 comparator so you can see baseline vs current selection. mock: https://img.redwood.internal/tmp/heatmap-timepicker-v2.png :sparkles:

kevin (product): Nice! Two product asks: 1) keep "Last 1h / 24h / 7d" presets but add a custom range quick-toggle, 2) make the baseline p95 persist across navigations (so PMs can pin the baseline).

rik (eng): Implementation note: folding heatmap to sparkline should reuse the same aggregated buckets server-side. front-end should request lower-resolution tiles for small widths. Also watch out for token-level cost when loading full heatmaps across many orgs.

ana (ux): (typo) meant to say ana. +1 on persistent baseline — we'll add a pin icon. For the timepicker, i propose a small "granularity" hint under the selected range: e.g., "granularity: 1m buckets" so users know sampling assumptions.

tess (a11y): Accessibility: the presets must be keyboard-focusable and have aria-pressed state. For the heatmap, ensure each cell has a focus target and an accessible label like "14:32 - 14:33: p95 312ms, 120 reqs". Color-only encoding for intensity is a problem — add a pattern overlay option or numeric tooltip.

kevin (product): Good catch — preference toggle for pattern overlay could live in the view menu. Also copy nit: change "p95 comparator" -> "p95 vs baseline". Clearer for external users.

rik (eng): For the p95 comparator line: if the time selection is short and spikes are sharp, the p95 graph can become noisy. Suggest we compute a smoothed moving-average overlay (configurable window 3-5 buckets). Also backend can return percentile CI so UI can show faint band around p95.

ana (ux): love the CI band idea — visually helps show uncertainty. Will include faint shaded band in mock. On small screens the comparator becomes a single stat card showing "p95 now: 420ms (+68ms vs baseline)".

opsbot: Reminder: deploy scheduled for staging at 2026-03-26T02:00Z. Feature-flag: heatmap-folding = off by default.

kevin (product): On sampling controls: we need an explicit label "Sampling for visualizations" and an explanation line: "Lowering sampling reduces client-side cost but may underrepresent rare spikes." Also support a "simulate" button to project how p95 might change at sample rates 100/50/10/1%.

tess (a11y): Simulate button must be reachable and announce progress to screen readers. Results should be presented as a table with plain text (no reliance on color).

rik (eng): Backend can run approximate replays for simulate, but it's expensive. Suggest we cache recent simulation results per-org and only re-run when selection or timeframe changes. Also cap simulation duration to last 7d by default.

ana (ux): UX detail: when sampling is < 20% show a subtle warning pill: "Low sampling may miss rare latency events" with a learn-more link. If auto-suggest is enabled we'll offer a recommended sampling % and a one-click apply.

kevin (product): Let's default auto-suggest off for new orgs but surface it in onboarding. Also track telemetry: when users accept suggested sampling and whether they pin baseline.

tess (a11y): Color contrast for heatmap palette on light theme is marginal; pick palettes that meet 4.5:1 when used with pattern overlays. Keyboard nav for heatmap cells should support arrow keys and Home/End to jump to edges.

rik (eng): I'll add keyboard coords handling in the component and optimize tile fetches. For the moving-average smoothing, we'll expose a toggle: "Show smoothed p95". Default off.

ana (ux): next steps: i'll update the prototypes with pinned baseline, CI band, low-sample warning pill, and the simulate modal. Will annotate all interactive targets with 8px minimum hit area. Posting updated prototype link in ~3h.

opsbot: Task checklist created: UX updates, Backend simulate caching, Heatmap accessibility audit, Telemetry events.

kevin (product): thanks all — please drop PR links when ready. small follow-up: can the timepicker support deep links (url params) so customers can share views with baseline/preset selected?

rik (eng): yes, we can serialize {range, baselinePinned, sampling} in the querystring; watch for length limits.

ana (ux): perfect. closing loop — prototype will include shareable URL example. (reacts :raised_hands:)
